sections.heading: Free Will And Pattern
sections.body: The chart describes urges, patterns, inclinations, and developmental material. It does not remove choice. User-facing text should translate chart symbolism into awareness and agency: this is the pattern, this is how it can run unconsciously, and this is how the user can work with it.

sections.heading: Interpretation Order
sections.body: Begin with the whole chart before details: element and mode balance, hemispheres and quadrants, angular emphasis, chart shape, luminaries, Ascendant and chart ruler, house rulers, then major aspects. Do not let a single placement dominate the reading unless the chart repeats it.

sections.heading: Planet As Function
sections.body: Planets describe psychological functions: identity, emotion, thought, desire, action, growth, structure, change, imagination, and transformation. Signs describe style and temperament. Houses describe the life area. Aspects describe how functions cooperate, resist, pressure, or integrate.

sections.heading: Houses As Developmental Fields
sections.body: Houses should be read as fields of experience, not static labels. A planet in a house shows where that planetary function is being practiced, challenged, and made visible in life. Rulers connect one house topic to another and should be used for personalization.

sections.heading: Moon Phases And Nodes
sections.body: Natal Moon phase gives developmental tone: beginning, building, testing, culmination, sharing, revision, or release. The lunar nodes describe familiar patterns and growth direction. Do not make the nodes deterministic; use them to describe what is easy to repeat and what asks for development.

sections.heading: Comparison Before Synastry
sections.body: Before comparing charts, read each person's natal capacity for relationship. Then compare luminaries, Ascendant, personal planets, Saturn, nodes, house overlays, and repeated themes. A relationship reading should explain dynamics without assigning fate or obligation.

sections.heading: Plain-Language Spirituality
sections.body: Spiritual language should stay grounded. Translate symbolic material into lived questions: what pattern is being repeated, what skill is being developed, what responsibility belongs to the user, and what choice is available now.
